gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::Filter + Insn::FilterAdd (bloom-filter build/probe pair)
gaps.notes: Turso builds a bloom filter over a join/IN side and probes it to skip btree seeks. Ahtola has no bloom machinery. NAME COLLISION: Ahtola's VdbeOpcode.Filter (12) is a row-predicate filter (VdbeRowPredicate delegate), NOT the bloom-filter probe — any port must rename. Pure optimization: results stay correct without it.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::HashBuild, HashDistinct, HashBuildFinalize, HashProbe, HashNext, HashClose, HashClear, HashMarkMatched, HashResetMatched, HashScanUnmatched, HashNextUnmatched, HashGraceInit, HashLoadPartition, HashNextProbe, HashAdvancePartition (16 opcodes; turso-src/core/vdbe/hash_table.rs)
gaps.notes: Entire hash-join execution family absent, including the grace (disk-partitioned) variant for outsized build sides and the unmatched-scan support for outer joins. Ahtola joins are in-memory nested loops over materialized rows (VdbeJoinPlan/OpenJoinCursor), so large equijoins degrade. The triple-selfjoin conformance timeouts are planner-caused (no cost-based ordering) but hash join is the execution-side fix.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::VOpen, VFilter, VColumn, VNext, VUpdate, VDestroy, VBegin, VRename (turso-src/core/vtab.rs)
gaps.notes: No virtual-table opcode family at all: modules cannot be opened, filtered with constraint push-down (xBestIndex), column-read, updated, or renamed. Blocks the entire eponymous/module vtab SQL surface. All 5 vtab conformance failures trace here (parser accepts CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE per parser-layer entry, execution cannot run it).

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::Program, Gosub, Return, BeginSubrtn (trigger/FK sub-program invocation and subroutine call/return)
gaps.notes: No subprogram or subroutine machinery: triggers cannot fire from compiled DML because there is no Program opcode to invoke a sub-program with its own register frame, and no Gosub/Return for shared code blocks. Ahtola programs are straight-line with explicit targets; subroutines are inlined at compile time. Prerequisite for any trigger support.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_halt (err_code + description + on_error + description_reg for RAISE); op_halt_if_null
gaps.ahtola_ref: src/Ahtola.Core/Execution/ResumableStatement.cs (case HaltInstruction, ~line 1139: clean stop, cursor cleanup only)
gaps.notes: Turso's Halt terminates with a SQLite error code, message, and on_error disposition (abort/ignore/fail), and HaltIfNull raises constraint errors from NULL registers (RAISE, NOT NULL). Ahtola's HaltInstruction only stops cleanly; all errors propagate as .NET exceptions (EmbeddedSqlException/VdbeArithmeticException) and are mapped to SQLite codes at the provider boundary (SqliteException.SqliteErrorCode). Works for top-level errors but cannot express in-program error recovery (ON CONFLICT CONTINUE semantics inside a program) or RAISE().

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_transaction (read/write flag, schema-cookie check, statement-tx sub-state machine); op_autocommit
gaps.notes: Different factoring, verified semantics: Ahtola splits into Begin/Commit/Rollback opcodes over VdbeTransaction (register-snapshot stack) with savepoint trio Savepoint/Release/RollbackTo mapping Turso's single Savepoint opcode with op enum. NAME COLLISION: Ahtola's VdbeOpcode.Commit is a cursor-write flush (returns LastInsertRowId), not a transaction commit. Isolation/atomicity gaps are in the mvcc layer entries, not here.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::Insn::OpenEphemeral, OpenAutoindex (execute.rs ~line 13467), OpenPseudo, OpenDup
gaps.notes: No general-purpose ephemeral btree opcode: Turso materializes IN (...) sets, DISTINCT intermediates, subquery results, and auto-indexes into ephemeral tables with full cursor semantics (seek/scan). Ahtola's only ephemeral store is the recursive-CTE work table; IN-list materialization and subquery materialization fall back to in-memory arrays/delegates, which caps planner options (no ephemeral index over a materialized subquery). OpenPseudo/OpenDup are minor conveniences Ahtola does not need structurally.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::OpenAutoindex + translate/optimizer (automatic transient index over the inner side of a join)
gaps.notes: Turso can build a transient auto-index when no usable index exists for a join. Combined with the missing cost-based join order (compilation entry), Ahtola's joins are O(N*M) nested loops with materialized right sides.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_deferred_seek (line 5180) + op_seek_end (line 5739); op_column OpColumnState::Rowid/Seek deferred path (lines 1779-1833)
gaps.notes: DeferredSeek lets an index scan postpone the table-btree seek until a column outside the index is actually read (covering-index fast path); SeekEnd positions a cursor past the last row for append workloads. Ahtola always materializes the full row on cursor access (CurrentCursorRow), so there is no covering-index read path and no lazy seek.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::Insn::IdxGE, IdxGT, IdxLE, IdxLT (execute.rs ~line 5680), IdxRowId, IdxInsert (line 10499), IdxDelete (line 10380), RowData
gaps.ahtola_ref: src/Ahtola.Core/Compilation/SortedScanProgramBuilder.cs; index maintenance inside write-target delegates (no dedicated opcodes)
gaps.notes: Turso has a full index-cursor family: range seeks with eq_only over index records, rowid extraction from index entries, index insert/delete with IdxInsertFlags (no-op dup detection), and raw record access (RowData). Ahtola reaches indexes only through the SortedScan builder and maintains them inside DML delegates. Works for the compiled shapes but blocks index-only scans, IN-driven index seeks, and partial/expression index exploitation (see compilation entries).

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::Insn::SeekGE, SeekGT, SeekLE, SeekLT with eq_only (lines 5232-5300); Insn::Found, NotFound, NoConflict, NotExists
gaps.notes: Ahtola consolidates point seeks into SeekRowid (with Found/NotFound targets folded in — a faithful merge of SeekRowid+Found/NotFound) and has SeekRowidRange for rowid ranges, but has no record-key seeks (SeekGE/GT/LE/LT over arbitrary index keys) and no eq_only distinction, and no NoConflict/NotExists probe opcodes (uniqueness is enforced inside write delegates instead). SeekRowidInstruction's own doc comment notes its scaffolding 'is not yet emitted by SelectStatementCompiler' — the opcode exists but the compiler never uses it (dead opcode today).

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::RowSetTest (dedup probe: jump if rowid already in set)
gaps.notes: Ahtola's RowSet trio maps Turso's RowSetAdd/RowSetRead (insert + drain) but lacks RowSetTest, the membership probe used to deduplicate rowids from OR'd index scans. Without it, multi-index OR plans cannot dedup — consistent with the compilation-layer finding that OR-index-union plans are absent.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_make_record (line 2746: serial-type encoding into SQLite record format); op_type_check (line 2023)
gaps.ahtola_ref: src/Ahtola.Core/Execution (registers hold SqlValue[] rows; record encoding happens at the pager write boundary); src/Ahtola.Core/Execution/VdbeProgram.cs::NumericAffinityInstruction, CastInstruction
gaps.notes: No MakeRecord: Ahtola rows live as materialized SqlValue arrays end-to-end and are only encoded to SQLite record format by the pager when a page is written. Format parity is a storage-layer concern (verified there); the VDBE-level consequence is that affinity-on-write (Turso's TypeCheck applying column affinities + CHECKs to a record before insert) happens in Ahtola's write delegates instead — see vdbe-typecheck-on-write.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_type_check (applies column affinities to a register block and enforces CHECK constraints before MakeRecord/Insert)
gaps.notes: Turso centralizes write-time coercion in TypeCheck; Ahtola scatters it across write delegates and the compiler's NumericAffinityInstruction emission. The 148-case wrong-values conformance cluster (affinity.sqltest leads it) shows the current placement misses cases — e.g. affinity through expression shapes the compiler does not annotate. Not an opcode-port job per se: the fix is making the compiler/delegate emission match TypeCheck's coverage matrix.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::NewRowid (max+1 allocation with random-retry fallback at i64::MAX; separate from last_insert_rowid tracking)
gaps.ahtola_ref: src/Ahtola.Core/Execution/ResumableStatement.cs (CommitInstruction: LastInsertRowId = target.Commit(), ~line 631); rowid allocation inside write targets
gaps.notes: Rowid allocation is delegated to the write target's Commit rather than a NewRowid opcode. The autoinc failure (explicit max-rowid insert followed by plain INSERT) suggests the allocation edge (SQLite falls back to random unused rowid when max is reached; AUTOINCREMENT must error instead) is not faithfully reproduced. Verify SQLITE_FULL-vs-random behavior when porting.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_insert (line 9897: InsertFlags::REQUIRE_SEEK, UPDATE_ROWID_CHANGE, PREFER_UPDATE; old-record capture for dependent views); op_delete (line 10274)
gaps.notes: Ahtola models UPDATE as its own opcode plus delegate mutation, with change counting present. Missing flag semantics: REQUIRE_SEEK (position-before-write), UPDATE_ROWID_CHANGE (rowid-changing UPDATE ordering), PREFER_UPDATE (upsert resolution hint). The MVCC-layer finding that statement-level rollback after ON CONFLICT ROLLBACK on UPDATE is broken compounds here: conflict disposition is decided inside delegates with no flag channel.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_comparison (line 888: Eq/Ne/Lt/Le/Gt/Ge as direct conditional jumps with CmpInsFlags {null_eq, jump_if_null, affinity, collation})
gaps.notes: Verified near-parity consolidation: Ahtola evaluates the comparison to a tri-state value (IS/IS NOT handled null-safely; NULL -> NULL; affinities applied per side; collation passed) then branches on IsTrue. jump_if_null maps to NULL->false->FalseTarget; null_eq maps to the IS operator. Residual risks: (1) EmbeddedDatabase.IsTrue throws 'datatype mismatch' for non-numeric text where SQLite treats it as false; (2) JumpIfInstruction (~line 693) silently treats text as not-jumping — inconsistent with IsTrue. Recorded for completeness; fix the two IsTrue edges rather than de-consolidating.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::Insn::IfPos, IfNeg, DecrJumpZero, MustBeInt (line 10943), ZeroOrNull, SoftNull (line 10961), MemMax (line 2788), AddImm, HaltIfNull (line 3262), Once, Noop
gaps.ahtola_ref: none (compiler inlines equivalent logic via gates/delegates)
gaps.notes: Mostly compiler machinery Ahtola's different program shapes do not need (counter loops, init-once blocks). Two carry user-visible semantics that deserve a check when the surrounding features land: MustBeInt (coerce-or-'datatype mismatch' used on rowid/FK paths) and HaltIfNull (RAISE/NOT NULL violation entry point). MemMax feeds AUTOINCREMENT sequence tracking.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_column (lines 1903-1925: record with fewer columns than schema -> column DEFAULT value operand; null_flag -> NULL)
gaps.ahtola_ref: src/Ahtola.Core/Execution/VdbeProgram.cs::ColumnInstruction (~line 1329: 'Retrieval of a missing column yields NULL')
gaps.notes: Turso's Column carries the column's DEFAULT as an operand so rows physically written before ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN read back the default. Ahtola's ColumnInstruction documents NULL for a missing column and has no default operand. alter.sqltest passes except FK cases, so the pager decode likely pads or the shapes tested do not hit short records with defaults — VERIFY: `ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN c TEXT DEFAULT 'x'` then SELECT c on pre-existing rows through the pager path. Also no NullRow opcode (LEFT JOIN null-fill is done by join delegates instead — structural, fine).

gaps.ahtola_ref: src/Ahtola.Core/Storage/SqliteWalWriterCheckpointCoordinator.cs (internal checkpoint machinery; no SQL/opcode entry point)
gaps.notes: Checkpoint coordination exists internally (storage layer) but there is no Checkpoint opcode, so `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(...)` has no execution path — directly causes the three wal_checkpoint conformance failures (stacked on the parser-layer pragma catch-all gap).

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::IntegrityCk (btree/record integrity walk driven from VDBE)
gaps.notes: PRAGMA integrity_check/quick_check needs the opcode-driven btree walk; Ahtola has no integrity checker. Pairs with the parser-layer pragma catch-all gap.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/explain.rs (SQLite-style EXPLAIN rows: addr/opcode/p1-p5/comment) + Insn::Explain (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN node text)
gaps.notes: Ahtola has a real EXPLAIN implementation over its own opcode set, so output necessarily diverges from SQLite/Turso text (different opcode names, no p1-p5 operand columns). Acceptable while EXPLAIN is diagnostic-only, but any conformance case asserting EXPLAIN output shape or EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN rows will fail. Decide policy: SQLite-emulating output vs documented Ahtola dialect.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::op_init_coroutine (9761), op_end_coroutine (9788), op_yield (9808); Insn::Init (init-block jump)
gaps.notes: Turso implements co-routines (FROM-clause subqueries, scalar subqueries, CTEs) as register-machine coroutines with Yield; Ahtola uses .NET enumerators and dedicated runtimes — a managed-idiom adaptation per the porting model. NAME COLLISION: Turso's Yield is a coroutine switch; Ahtola's ResultRow is the row-yield. Capability consequences (which subquery shapes materialize) are tracked in compilation entries, not here.

gaps.notes: Micro-opcodes: ResetSorter (re-drain a sorter for correlated subqueries without rebuilding), AggValue (read aggregate mid-iteration), OpenDup (cheap cursor clone), ColumnsUsed (column-usage metadata). OffsetLimit maps faithfully onto Ahtola's OffsetGate/LimitGate pair. None block SQL surface; each is a small perf/completeness item.

gaps.notes: CDC bootstrap opcode; feeds Turso's CDC capture consumed by sync. No Ahtola counterpart (sync layer lacks CDC too — see sync entries).

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/insn.rs::Insn::PopulateMaterializedViews; op_insert old-record capture for dependent views (execute.rs lines 9916-10019); op_column MaterializedView cursor arms
gaps.notes: Turso's incremental-materialized-view extension: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW, dependent-view capture in DML opcodes, MV cursor types. Parser layer confirms no Ahtola grammar. Upstream extension, not adopted.

gaps.turso_ref: none (Turso evaluates window functions via sorter + aggregate-style accumulation in translate/window.rs)
gaps.notes: Ahtola-only buffered-window evaluation: the whole partition is buffered, then computed in one pass, enabling forward-looking and peer-relative frames cleanly. Semantically ahead for the shapes it covers; window *coverage* gaps (frame types) are compilation entries.

gaps.turso_ref: none direct (Turso uses OpenEphemeral + coroutines for recursive CTEs; LIMIT/OFFSET via OffsetLimit; DISTINCT via ephemeral indexes)
gaps.ahtola_ref: src/Ahtola.Core/Execution/VdbeProgram.cs::OpenWorkTableInstruction, SeedWorkTableInstruction, WorkTableStepInstruction, WorkTableExpandInstruction, WorkTableExpandGenerationInstruction, CloseWorkTableInstruction; OffsetGate/LimitGate/DistinctGate/DistinctFilter/DistinctResultRow/CompoundResultRow/GuardedRow/SameGroup/GroupKey/ProjectRegisters/FilterRegisters/FilterRowId/RowCount/SeekRowidRange/OpenJoinCursor/Update/Commit/AggReset instructions
gaps.notes: Ahtola's higher-level opcode families: FIFO recursive work tables (recursive CTE), streaming join cursor, and gate opcodes that fuse what Turso does with primitive jump/compare sequences. These are the consolidation wins of the managed port — documented so the matrix does not misread them as unexplained divergence.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs op_agg_step (line ~6647): Sum/Avg/Total overflow and large-float accumulation semantics
gaps.notes: SUM/TOTAL/AVG over very large REAL values: Ahtola diverges from SQLite/Turso on infinity/overflow results for float aggregates. Verify Kahan/compensated summation and int->real promotion behavior against op_agg_step.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/join.rs::optimize_join_order (System R style DP), turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/mod.rs::optimize_plan
gaps.notes: Turso's optimizer/join.rs implements a System-R style dynamic-programming join reordering algorithm with pruning, using per-table cost/cardinality estimates (optimizer/cost.rs, cost_params.rs) and ANALYZE stats when present. Ahtola's VdbeJoinPlan always joins tables strictly in FROM/JOIN clause order (VdbeJoinOperatorPlan is a fixed left-deep tree built by the caller, not re-ordered by any cost model). Multi-table queries where writing the FROM clause in join order matters for performance will be correct but slow; there is no code path that reorders joins for a smaller intermediate result.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/access_method.rs::best_access_method, turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/constraints.rs
gaps.notes: Turso extracts WHERE-clause conjuncts into per-table Constraints and picks the cheapest access method (rowid seek, single/multi-column index seek, or full scan) per table independently of join order, considering multiple candidate indexes and their selectivity. Ahtola's ResolveScanTarget/IndexSemantics resolve at most one usable index per scan target via direct predicate-to-index matching (IndexExpressionSemantics.PredicateImplies/SplitConjuncts); there is no comparison between competing candidate indexes on the same table, no partial-index-aware cost comparison, and no multi-index intersection (Turso's optimizer/multi_index.rs, OR-clause index union) at all.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/multi_index.rs
gaps.notes: SQLite/Turso can satisfy `WHERE a=1 OR b=2` (with separate indexes on a and b) via an index-union/OR-optimization instead of a full scan. Ahtola's compiler has no equivalent: OR predicates in WHERE fall back to sequential scan filtering (FilterRegistersInstruction), never index lookups per OR-branch.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/order.rs::eliminate_order_by, turso-src/core/translate/order_by.rs
gaps.notes: Turso's order.rs decides, per join order and access method, whether the chosen index already produces the required ORDER BY/GROUP BY order and elides the sort step. Ahtola only special-cases a single ORDER BY term matching the primary key/rowid for a single-table backward scan (SelectStatementCompiler ~line 132); any other case -- including index-satisfied ORDER BY on a secondary index, or GROUP BY order elision -- always materializes through a Sorter (SortedScanProgramBuilder). The listed conformance failures show sort-elision expectations not met for window/CTE queries.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/select.rs (join emission uses per-node OpenRead/Seek via chosen access method)
gaps.notes: VdbeJoinOperatorPlan.Enumerate always materializes the right side fully and nested-loops the left side against it in memory (VdbeJoinRow arrays), regardless of whether an index exists on the join key. There is no index-driven nested-loop join (seek into the right table per left row using its index) anywhere in the join plan machinery -- every N-way join is O(preceding-rows * table-size) in the worst case. JoinProgramBuilder.cs (2-table direct builder) is explicitly nested-loop only per its own doc comment.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/optimizer/access_method.rs, cost.rs (equi-join cost modeling; Turso does not implement a hash-join operator either, but its cost model reasons about equi-join constraints for index seeks)
gaps.notes: Neither engine implements a true hash-join operator (both fundamentally rely on nested-loop plus index seeks), so this is not a gap versus Turso per se, but flagged because Ahtola's total absence of index-driven joins (see compile-nway-join-not-index-driven) means large equi-joins have no efficient path at all, whereas Turso's cost model at least picks an index seek that approximates hash-join performance for the common case.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/subquery.rs (recursive CTE planning, multiple recursive terms via compound UNION legs), turso-src/core/translate/compound_select.rs
gaps.notes: RecursiveCteProgramBuilder explicitly documents its scope as "the well-defined linear recursion (a single recursive transform)" and states "Multiple distinct recursive terms ... and mutual recursion are out of scope". `WITH RECURSIVE cte AS (anchor UNION leg1 UNION leg2 ...)` (3+ compound terms) fails to parse/compile ("Expected RightParen"), confirmed by the cte_expressions.sqltest failures.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/subquery.rs, planner.rs (FROM-clause subquery flattening / pull-up into the outer query)
gaps.ahtola_ref: none (subqueries are always compiled as independently executed/materialized nested queries; see EmbeddedDatabase.cs::MaterializeSubqueryResult line ~23552)
gaps.notes: SQLite/Turso can flatten many `FROM (SELECT ...)` derived-table subqueries into the outer query when safe (no aggregates/DISTINCT/LIMIT conflicts), avoiding a materialization step and letting the outer WHERE clause push predicates into the inner query and use its indexes. Ahtola has no flattening pass: every derived-table/subquery source is executed and materialized independently via MaterializeSubqueryResult/ExecuteQuery before the outer query consumes its rows, so predicates never push down into subquery index selection.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/subquery.rs::plan_subqueries_from_where_clause / plan_subqueries_with_outer_query_access (allow_correlated, hoists uncorrelated subqueries to execute once)
gaps.notes: Turso's subquery.rs distinguishes correlated from uncorrelated subqueries and hoists uncorrelated ones to evaluate once instead of once per outer row. Ahtola recomputes scalar/EXISTS/IN subqueries per outer row unconditionally (no correlation analysis found in EmbeddedDatabase.cs or the Compilation builders), which is correct but can be significantly slower for uncorrelated subqueries in a WHERE clause evaluated over many outer rows.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/select.rs, planner.rs (unified plan covers arbitrary joins/subqueries/aggregates through one planner)
gaps.notes: SelectStatementCompiler is architected as a set of narrow, provably-correct single-table fast paths (plain scan, backward/descending scan, indexed seek with bounds) with everything else falling through to more general (and slower) machinery in EmbeddedDatabase.cs/CompiledJoinProgramBuilder. This is a deliberate incremental-porting strategy (per repo convention of many small direct VDBE builders) rather than Turso's single unified planner, and is flagged as intentional/architectural rather than a functional bug.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/translate/upsert.rs::emit_upsert (upsert target resolution independent of INSERT source shape)
gaps.notes: Ahtola's UPSERT compiler rejects any INSERT...SELECT or CTE-sourced INSERT with an ON CONFLICT clause: "Managed UPSERT supports VALUES rows only and does not support INSERT ... gaps.notes: SqliteBtreeSplitMutation's own doc comment states it 'can replace existing pages or append new pages, but never shrinks, rebalances, or reclaims pages.' Turso's Pager::allocate_page consults the freelist trunk chain first (ReuseFreelistLeaf state) before growing the file. Practical effect: every DELETE/DROP in Ahtola leaves file space that is never reused by subsequent INSERTs outside of a full VACUUM rewrite, so the main database file only ever grows (bloat), unlike stock SQLite/Turso.

There is no free_page()-equivalent invoked when a b-tree page becomes empty during ordinary DELETE/DROP TABLE transactions, so the freelist is only ever populated/consumed as a side effect of a full rewrite, not incrementally as SQLite/Turso do.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/mvcc/mod.rs, turso-src/core/mvcc/database/mod.rs::MvStore, RowVersion, Transaction, TransactionState, turso-src/core/mvcc/clock.rs::MvccClock, turso-src/core/mvcc/cursor.rs, turso-src/core/mvcc/persistent_storage/logical_log.rs
gaps.notes: Turso implements a full main-memory MVCC engine (Larson et al., VLDB 2011) alongside its classic SQLite-compatible pager/b-tree path, selected per-transaction via `BEGIN CONCURRENT` (see execute.rs::begin_mvcc_tx, TransactionMode::Concurrent) rather than a global PRAGMA. Core pieces: (1) MvStore (database/mod.rs, ~10k lines) owns an in-memory multi-version row store keyed by RowID, with RowVersion carrying begin_ts/end_ts (TxTimestampOrID) and a RowVersionState (Committed/Uncommitted/Aborted-like states); (2) MvccClock (clock.rs) is a mutex-guarded logical clock generating monotonically increasing begin/commit timestamps, with a documented 'speculative reads' protocol so an active tx can observe another tx's writes once it enters the Preparing state even before it fully commits (atomicity between get_timestamp and publishing the Preparing state closes a TOCTOU snapshot-isolation hole the maintainers hit once already); (3) first-committer-wins conflict detection returns LimboError::WriteWriteConflict on commit when a concurrent writer touched the same row, so the caller must retry/rollback (see the busy-retry loops in mvcc/mod.rs tests); (4) a dual cursor (cursor.rs, MvccCursorType::Table/Index) that transparently overlays the MVCC version store on top of the classic b-tree cursor, promoting a plain btree cursor into an MVCC-aware one lazily (execute.rs::maybe_promote_to_mvcc_cursor); (5) a logical_log persistent_storage layer (persistent_storage/logical_log.rs, ~8k lines) that durably logs the version store's operations rather than paging rows through the WAL directly, plus a checkpoint_state_machine (database/checkpoint_state_machine.rs) that periodically folds the logical log into the b-tree/WAL so a restart can rebuild the MVCC store; (6) garbage collection via drop_unused_row_versions[/_and_slots] which prunes row versions no longer visible to any active transaction, invoked opportunistically from the commit path. Isolation level is snapshot isolation with read-your-writes and dirty-write/dirty-read prevention by construction (version visibility check before update), but the module's own doc header states phantom reads, cursor lost updates, read skew, and write skew are explicit unresolved TODOs upstream, and optimistic reads/writes plus GC are still marked incomplete even in the reference implementation. Two data paths coexist per-connection: ordinary BEGIN/BEGIN IMMEDIATE/BEGIN DEFERRED still go through the pager/WAL/b-tree exactly as classic SQLite; only BEGIN CONCURRENT engages MvStore, and mixing the two on the same table within one process requires the promotion/cursor-overlay machinery so a concurrent reader on a b-tree cursor does NOT see an uncommitted MVCC writer's row (test_mvcc_dual_cursor_transaction_isolation demonstrates this explicitly: a second BEGIN CONCURRENT connection sees the pre-MVCC-commit b-tree value, not the in-flight MVCC value). Ahtola has zero equivalent: no `*Mvcc*.cs` file exists anywhere in src/, `BEGIN CONCURRENT` is not a recognized parser production (fails with a generic 'Expected End' parse error per the conformance corpus), and every transaction — read or write — goes through the single pager-lock/WAL/rollback-journal path described in EmbeddedTransactionLock.cs, SqliteWalReadSnapshotCoordinator.cs, SqliteWalWriterCheckpointCoordinator.cs, and SqliteRollbackJournal.cs. Ahtola's model is therefore SQLite's classic single-writer/multiple-reader locking discipline exclusively: a single write reservation gate (EmbeddedTransactionLock, process-local, modeling SQLite's RESERVED/EXCLUSIVE locks with FIFO fairness for explicit transactions and barging for autocommit statements) and per-reader WAL snapshots (SqliteWalReadSnapshot pinning a committed WAL frame boundary) rather than a true multi-writer optimistic-concurrency layer. Adopting Turso's MVCC design would require: a new in-memory versioned row store keyed by (table, rowid) with begin/commit timestamps; a logical clock with the same atomicity guarantee as MvccClock; a write-write conflict detector integrated into VDBE Insert/Update/Delete opcode execution; a dual-cursor overlay so classic-path and MVCC-path connections observe correct visibility against each other; a durable logical-log + checkpoint-into-WAL story so MVCC state survives restart; row-version garbage collection; and new parser/VDBE support for `BEGIN CONCURRENT` as a per-transaction mode alongside the existing DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE. This is a multi-week/-month undertaking (L effort, likely several L-sized sub-projects) and is reasonably deferrable relative to correctness gaps elsewhere, since Ahtola's classic-path transactions already give SQLite-compatible single-writer serializable-enough semantics for the vast majority of consumer workloads; it is filed s2-capability (a real missing capability, not yet proven to be an intentional non-goal) pending an explicit product decision to scope it out.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs::TransactionMode::Concurrent, begin_mvcc_tx, line ~3819 'Concurrent transaction mode is only supported when MVCC is enabled'
gaps.notes: Turso recognizes BEGIN CONCURRENT as a transaction-mode keyword and, even when MVCC is disabled, produces the specific error 'Concurrent transaction mode is only supported when MVCC is enabled' (execute.rs ~3819-3822) rather than a parse failure. Ahtola's parser has no CONCURRENT production at all, so the same SQL text fails earlier and differently ('Expected End. At SQL offset 6'), which is itself a conformance divergence independent of whether MVCC is ever implemented: four expected-failure lines exist purely because the error message/shape differs, not because of missing MVCC semantics. A cheap partial fix (M effort) is to at least parse BEGIN CONCURRENT and raise the same not-supported message Turso gives when MVCC is off, improving message-compatibility without implementing the feature.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/mvcc/clock.rs::MvccClock, LogicalClock::get_timestamp/get_commit_timestamp
gaps.notes: Turso's MvccClock is a mutex-guarded monotonic counter where the commit-timestamp generation and publication of the transaction's Preparing(ts) state happen atomically under one lock (documented at length in clock.rs to close a proven snapshot-isolation TOCTOU bug from an earlier lock-free attempt, turso#5198). Ahtola has no logical clock concept in its transaction model; its WAL snapshot coordinator (SqliteWalReadSnapshotCoordinator.cs) pins a *frame* boundary rather than a logical timestamp, which is adequate for the classic pager path but has no analogue for a future MVCC begin_ts/commit_ts scheme. Any MVCC implementation must budget for this atomicity requirement explicitly, not bolt a naive counter on afterward.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/mvcc/database/mod.rs::LimboError::WriteWriteConflict (raised at multiple sites, e.g. lines ~1843, ~1865-1976, ~2798, ~5191-5227)
gaps.notes: Turso's MVCC path detects first-committer-wins write-write conflicts and surfaces LimboError::WriteWriteConflict distinctly from Busy, so callers can decide whether to retry (Busy, lock contention) or must restart the transaction with new reads (WriteWriteConflict, logical conflict). Ahtola's whole-database EmbeddedTransactionLock model makes write-write conflicts structurally impossible to observe as a distinct error: only one writer can ever hold the reservation at a time, so overlapping writers serialize via EmbeddedBusyException (SQLITE_BUSY) rather than racing and one aborting after the fact. This is consistent with the classic single-writer model and not a bug, but it means Ahtola cannot express Turso's MVCC concurrent-write semantics (multiple writers proceeding optimistically) without introducing this conflict-detection concept.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/mvcc/database/mod.rs::drop_unused_row_versions, drop_unused_row_versions_and_slots, drop_unused_row_versions_inner (lines ~6995-7275)
gaps.notes: Turso's MVCC store accumulates multiple row versions per key and periodically garbage-collects versions no longer visible to any active transaction (three-rule pruning, driven opportunistically from the commit path and test loops). This has no Ahtola analogue because there is no version store to garbage-collect; filed separately from mvcc-layer-absent because it is a distinct sub-component (memory-management policy) that any future MVCC port must budget for independently — a naive port that skips GC will leak memory under sustained concurrent write load.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs (Transaction/AutoCommit opcode arms, TransactionMode::None/Read/Write/Concurrent)
gaps.notes: Ahtola's actual (non-MVCC) transaction model is itself undocumented at a design level: it is a single process-local write reservation (EmbeddedTransactionLock, one lock per file-backed database keyed by canonicalized path via EmbeddedTransactionLockRegistry, or one per in-memory database instance) that models SQLite's RESERVED/EXCLUSIVE locks, with FIFO fairness for explicit-transaction writers (Enter) but barging for autocommit statements (EnterAutocommit) to avoid a documented starvation bug (ENGINE #17, EF migrations-lock convoy). Readers pin a WAL frame/page-count snapshot via SqliteWalReadSnapshotCoordinator/SqliteWalReadSnapshot rather than a logical timestamp. SqlTransactionControl.cs is a lightweight lexical scanner (not a parser integration) that Ahtola.Data uses to detect COMMIT/END/ROLLBACK[ TO] keywords in raw SQL text for ADO.NET-level transaction bookkeeping. None of this is written down anywhere as a coherent isolation-level statement (e.g. 'Ahtola provides snapshot-isolated reads against a single active writer, equivalent to SQLite's default WAL-mode semantics'); this entry exists to flag that documentation gap alongside the code gaps, since accurately characterizing the current model was itself part of this audit's scope.

gaps.turso_ref: turso-src/core/vdbe/execute.rs (Transaction/Savepoint opcode arms operate on real pager/MVCC state)

This is intentional and correctly documented, but a gap-analysis reader could easily mistake this file for Ahtola's real transaction manager since its name and API (Begin/Commit/Rollback/Savepoint/Release/RollbackTo) mirror SQL transaction control precisely. Filed as s4-intentional/no-action purely to record that the real transaction/lock/snapshot logic lives in EmbeddedTransactionLock.cs + the WAL coordinators + EmbeddedDatabase.cs's statement execution, not here.

This means Ahtola's UPDATE path cannot currently terminate an entire transaction as a side effect of a single row's constraint violation, a capability gap distinct from (and layered on top of) the SAVEPOINT/BEGIN/COMMIT mechanics that do work.

gaps.ahtola_ref: none (no CheckpointMode consumer in Ahtola.Data sync path; Ahtola.Core WAL checkpoint is out of this layer's scope)
gaps.notes: Turso's sync checkpoint explicitly composes Passive (checkpoint only the already-synced WAL prefix, tracked by a watermark) followed by Truncate (once fully synced) to keep the revert-DB's WAL valid relative to the main DB file. Since Ahtola has no sync engine consuming Ahtola.Core's checkpoint modes for this purpose, there is no equivalent watermark-aware checkpoint orchestration layered on top of Ahtola.Core's WAL/pager; flagged here as the sync-layer half of a gap whose storage-layer half belongs to the storage-format-port skill.
